root_cause: The movement planner mis-prices a capture trip's REACH, and every downstream term inherits the error. (a) On 11e terrain objectives (14.01: the hosting AREA is the objective; all three findings' centres are ruin pairs) gap_in is still centroid -> marker point minus 3" (FIX-HELD-DUP only fixed the 'already on it' test). At s7462 r1 P2 Lootas Alpha's centroid is 19.6" from the centre marker (gap 15.8" -> 2 turns) but its nearest model is 7.3" from the centre's hosting area. (b) A trip the plan Advances on because the Advance reaches range THIS turn (gap in (M, M+2]) is still costed ceil(gap/M) = 2 turns. The overstated turns_to_reach turned the centre into a 2-turn trip: contest_race x0.5 (-13.85), distance penalty, -2 reachability, and LONE-TRIP's 2-move race window (~30 enemy OC vs our 10 -> veto) instead of now + next move (~5 OC). With the centre vetoed the unit got a 3-turn trip to obj_nml_1 and T7-26 then held it still (its 'reachable' test also reads centroid -> marker). Evidence: branch B (Advance to centre) reached the centre's area in ONE Advance in both seeds and held it at P2's next Command phase (+4 hold_more, P1 lost its hold_min): A -7/-4 vs B +4/+7 (seeds 5001/5002). F2 (s7463, centre 12.1" from its area: a real 2-turn trip) and F3 (11.9") are not explained by the reach error: there the centre is a genuine 2-turn race that LONE-TRIP vetoes / T7-26 holds for.
fix_summary: FIX_RANGED_CENTRE (default 1; 0 = base exactly). In _assign_units_to_objectives' candidate loop, for a unit not already on the objective: gap_in = min(marker gap, nearest alive model's MissionManager.model_gap_to_objective_range_px) when the objective has hosting areas (via FIX-HELD-DUP's hd_obj_by_id / hd_mm); turns_to_reach is recomputed from that gap; when the gap is in (M, M+2] and _should_unit_advance says Advance (computed once, reused by the action branch), turns_to_reach = 1. RACE-1's long-Advance pace, contest race, distance penalty, reachability, LONE-TRIP / RACE-SKIP / TOO-LATE all then read the corrected turns. Candidates carry gap_in; T7-26 _should_hold_for_heavy_bonus tests 'reachable this move' and 'high-priority within 2 moves' on that gap too. [RANGED_CENTRE] log (stdout + debug log) when an assigned move/advance is priced at fewer turns than the previous pricing, and when the Heavy hold is skipped because of the corrected gap. No special case for Lootas, round 1 or the centre.

fires: Replays (debug-log lines, both players, to the end of the next battle round; only 4 of the 8 fix replays' logs survived log rotation): 11 (f3, 2 Heavy-hold skips), 4, 5, 7 (g4 round 3, 2 Heavy-hold skips); F1/F2 logs showed the reprice firing for Lootas Gamma -> centre (MOVE 5.2", 1 turn vs 2), Lootas Alpha -> obj_nml_2, Battlewagons, Custodian Guard etc. Bench (mirror_orks_2000_postdeploy, 1 pair, seed 93101): 19 fires in each game (candidate seat only; M1: 11 MOVE + 8 ADVANCE reprices, M2: 10 MOVE + 9 ADVANCE, 0 Heavy-hold skips) - Stompa/Deffkoptas/Warbikers/Wazdakka trips to centre/NML/home priced 1 turn shorter. It fires broadly: it is a board-wide reach correction, not a Lootas trigger.
risks: (1) Broad: it reprices every unit's trips to terrain-hosted objectives (19 per bench game), so its full-game effect is not predicted by these single-position checks; the one bench pair went -7.5 VP for the candidate (lost both games; 1 pair is noise-level, but nothing positive was seen). (2) Asymmetry: our reach now uses the nearest model to the hosting area, the enemy's arrivals (race_enemy_oc, projected_enemy_oc, friendly_arrivals) still use centroid -> marker with M+2" slack, so contests look easier for us than for them; LONE-TRIP now judges 1-turn trips on next-move threat only, which can send fragile units forward into a flood arriving the turn after (the round-2 FAR_TRIP/OVERCOMMIT lesson in reverse). (3) Advance-now = 1 turn ignores the 1/6-1/3 chance the roll falls short and the lost shooting of an Advance for ranged units. (4) Execution may not match the price: the executor walks the centroid toward the marker; terrain walls or coherency can leave the front model off the area. (5) It redistributes objectives between units (F1: Gamma took the centre, Alpha went to obj_nml_2; F3: Alpha dropped to a corridor block), so a corrected price can reshuffle the plan into unmeasured assignments. (6) Heavy-hold skips cost the +1 to hit in later rounds when a unit is 'reachable' by gap but not really worth walking.
